title: Evaluate the inner value
text: First, calculate the inner value: what is $$\tan\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)?$$

subHints.title: Remember the range
subHints.text: The range of $$\arctan$$ is $$\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right).$$ It cannot return a value like $$\frac{3\pi}{4}.$$

subHints.title: Connection to the unit circle
subHints.text: Recall that $$\tan\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)$$ represents the slope of the line passing through the origin and the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{3\pi}{4}.$$

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle geometrically
subHints.text: The principal range of $$\arctan$$ is $$\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right), $$ which is the right half of the unit circle. To find an angle in this range that creates the same slope as $$\frac{3\pi}{4}, $$ extend that line straight through the origin into Quadrant IV. It hits the right half of the circle at $$-\frac{\pi}{4}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle algebraically
subHints.text: We can also solve this algebraically using the periodic nature of the tangent function. Tangent has a period of $$\pi, $$ meaning $$\tan(\theta)=\tan(\theta-\pi).$$ Subtracting the period gives $$\frac{3\pi}{4}-\pi=-\frac{\pi}{4}.$$ Since this is inside the principal range, it is our answer.
